summary: Path string utility that truncates an in-place string buffer at its last backslash directory separator, stripping the trailing file component. It validates both arguments, copies the input into a 512-byte scratch buffer with a bounded copy, force-terminates the buffer at the caller-supplied limit, then walks backward from the end of the string clearing bytes until it reaches a backslash. Callers include settings/profile loaders and profile-icon copy paths, consistent with a path-directory normalization helper.

local_names.v2: strlen(a1) + 1, the length-plus-NUL terminator used to compute the backward scan start
local_names.v5: 512-byte stack scratch buffer receiving the bounded copy of the input

operations.description: Guard on the arguments: when either the path pointer a1 or the length a2 is zero/null, return -1 immediately without touching the buffers.
Calls sub_568620 with the scratch-buffer size 512 before the copy; the callee's body is absent from the packet so its exact role (stack setup / guard) is unverified.
Bounded copy of the input path a1 into the 512-byte scratch buffer v5, limited to a2-1 bytes, via sub_587DD0 (a bounded string copy helper).
Force-terminates the path at the caller-supplied limit by writing a NUL byte at a1[a2-1], guarding against an unterminated buffer.
Computes v2 = strlen(a1) + 1, i.e. the string length including its terminator, which locates the last data byte at a1[v2-2].

Backward scan: starting at a1[v2-2] and walking down toward a1, each byte is cleared until a byte equal to backslash (ASCII 92) is found, at which point the loop breaks. This truncates the string at the last directory separator, dropping the trailing file/component.
Returns 0 on the successful truncation path after the backward scan completes.
